lesson.title: Build a REST API with FastAPI and Pydantic
lesson.goal: build a REST API with FastAPI: GET and POST endpoints with Pydantic models, run with uvicorn

sources.title: Build a REST API with FastAPI and Pydantic

steps.title: Install FastAPI and run hello world
steps.instructions: Run `pip install fastapi uvicorn`, create main.py with `app = FastAPI()` and an `@app.get("/")` root route returning a small dict. Start it with `uvicorn main:app --reload` and open the address uvicorn prints in your browser.

targets.caption: Create the FastAPI app instance
Decorator defining the root GET route
Server is up; open the printed address

explanations.topic: Uvicorn is the server that runs FastAPI apps
The @app.get decorator defines a path for the HTTP GET method
The "/" path is the root; visiting it calls the function
uvicorn main:app = file name : app variable
--reload makes the server restart automatically when files change

hints: Make sure both packages are installed: pip install fastapi uvicorn.
In main.py, import FastAPI, create app = FastAPI(), then decorate a function with @app.get("/") that returns a dict.
If you see 'Error loading ASGI app', check that the part before the colon matches your file name and the part after matches your variable name.
common_mistakes: Installing only fastapi and getting 'uvicorn: command not found'.
Running uvicorn from a different directory than main.py, causing 'Could not import module "main"'.
Mismatching names in main:app (e.g. variable called api but running main:app).
Forgetting the parentheses in FastAPI(), so app is the class, not an instance.
Typing main.py:app instead of main:app.

steps.title: Add POST endpoint for items
steps.instructions: Add a module-level `items = []` list and an `@app.post("/items")` function `create_item(item: str)` that appends the item and returns the list. With uvicorn running, POST an item via curl to the /items path on the address uvicorn printed, passing `?item=apple`.

targets.caption: Module-level list holding the items
POST endpoint at /items
Server log of the POST request

explanations.topic: What routes are: URLs your app responds to
Using separate routes to add or view to-do items
POST request to the /items path
A plain str function argument becomes a query parameter
Returning the whole list to see accumulated results
Passing the item as a query parameter in the curl URL

hints: Above your routes, create an empty list at module level so every request shares it.
Use the @app.post decorator with the path "/items" on a new function.
Give the function a parameter like item: str; FastAPI treats it as a query parameter, so append it to the list and return the list.
common_mistakes: Using @app.get instead of @app.post, so curl -X POST returns 405 Method Not Allowed.
Defining items = [] inside the function, which resets the list on every request.
Omitting ?item=... from the URL, causing a 422 'field required' response.
Forgetting the single quotes around the URL, so the shell mangles the ? query string.
Not restarting uvicorn (or not using --reload), so the new route returns 404 Not Found.
Returning nothing from the function, so the response is null instead of the list.

steps.title: Add GET item by ID route
steps.instructions: Add `@app.get("/items/{item_id}")` with `get_item(item_id: int)` returning `items[item_id]`. Since the list resets on reload, POST two items again, then curl GET the /items/0 path on the uvicorn address.

targets.caption: Route with a path parameter
Type hint converts path value to int
Request the first item by index

explanations.topic: Path parameters: {item_id} in the route maps to a function argument
Server reload resets the in-memory items list
Whatever is in the URL becomes the item_id variable
Type hints make FastAPI convert the path value's type

hints: Use the same @app.get decorator as before, but put a variable name in curly brackets in the path.
The function argument name must match the name inside the curly brackets, and add an int type hint.
Return items[item_id]. Before testing, POST an item again because the reload emptied the list.
common_mistakes: Testing right after saving without re-POSTing items. The reload reset the list, so index 0 raises an IndexError (500).
Leaving out the int type hint, so item_id is a string and items[item_id] fails with a TypeError.
The function parameter name doesn't match the {placeholder} in the path.
Using /items/1 to get the first item. Indexes start at 0.
steps.run_command:
curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=apple'
curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=orange'
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/items/0

steps.title: Raise 404 with HTTPException
steps.instructions: In main.py import HTTPException from fastapi and in get_item return the item if item_id < len(items), else raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=...). Request a missing index with curl to see the 404 detail.

targets.caption: Import HTTPException from fastapi
Raise a 404 when the item is missing
The request now returns a useful 404 detail

explanations.topic: Why an internal server error is unhelpful
HTTP status codes and client errors
404 Not Found for missing items
HTTPException status_code and detail parameters

hints: FastAPI has a built-in exception class for returning HTTP errors. Import it from fastapi at the top of the file.
In get_item, check whether item_id is a valid index (item_id < len(items)) before indexing the list.
If the item doesn't exist, use raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=...) instead of return.
Re-run the same curl request for an index past the end of the list. You should see {"detail": "Item N not found"}.
common_mistakes: Using `return HTTPException(...)` instead of `raise`, which sends back a 200 response instead of a 404.
Forgetting to import HTTPException, which causes a NameError when the missing item is requested.
Using `<=` instead of `<` in the bounds check, which still triggers an IndexError for item_id == len(items).
Not restarting uvicorn (or not running it with --reload), so the old 500 error still appears.
Writing the detail as a plain string without the f prefix, so {item_id} isn't interpolated.

steps.title: List items with limit parameter
steps.instructions: In main.py add `@app.get("/items")` with `def list_items(limit: int = 10): return items[0:limit]`. With `uvicorn main:app --reload` running and a few items added, run `curl "localhost:8000/items?limit=3"` in a second terminal.

targets.caption: New GET /items endpoint with a limit query parameter
Request only the first 3 items

explanations.topic: Query parameters vs. path parameters
FastAPI converts query strings to the annotated type (int)
Same URL, different HTTP method routes to a different function
Default value in the function signature is used when limit is omitted

hints: Create a new function decorated with @app.get on the same "/items" path you used for POST.
Give the function a parameter limit annotated as int with a default of 10. FastAPI treats it as a query parameter.
Return a slice of the list: items[0:limit].
common_mistakes: Using @app.post instead of @app.get, so the request hits the create endpoint.
Forgetting the int type hint, which leaves limit as a string and breaks the slice.
Not quoting the URL in the shell, so the ? or & is interpreted by the shell.
Restarting the server without --reload, which empties the in-memory list, so the response is [].

steps.title: Use Pydantic Item model
steps.instructions: Import BaseModel from pydantic, define class Item(BaseModel) with text: str and is_done: bool = False, and make create_item accept item: Item. POST JSON with curl and note a missing text fails validation.

targets.caption: Pydantic model for a to-do item
Boolean field with a default
Response is an object matching the model

explanations.topic: Why Pydantic models: structure, validation, docs, completion
Model arguments are read from the JSON payload, not query params
Default field values (is_done false)
Removing a default makes a field required and validated

hints: Import BaseModel from pydantic and subclass it to make an Item class with two typed fields.
Give is_done a default of False; change the create_item parameter type from str to Item.
Send the item as JSON: add -H "Content-Type: application/json" and -d '{"text":"apple"}', and drop the ?item= query parameter from the URL.
To make text required, remove its default value; posting {"title":"apple"} should then return a validation error.
common_mistakes: Still sending the item as a query parameter (?item=apple), which gives a 422 because the model expects a JSON body.
Forgetting the Content-Type: application/json header in curl.
Using double quotes around the -d JSON in a shell without escaping the inner quotes.
Not restarting uvicorn (no --reload) so the old string-based endpoint still runs.
Writing class Item: without inheriting from BaseModel.

steps.title: Add response models to routes
steps.instructions: In main.py, add `response_model=Item` to the get_item decorator and `response_model=list[Item]` to the list_items decorator. Let uvicorn reload and confirm responses still return Item objects.

targets.caption: Response model on the get-item route
Response model on the list-items route

explanations.topic: Modeling responses with the same Pydantic BaseModel
response_model argument in the route decorator
Response models tell clients/interfaces what an endpoint returns

hints: The change goes in the decorators (@app.get(...)), not in the function bodies.
Add a keyword argument named response_model to each GET decorator.
For a single item use response_model=Item; for the list route use response_model=list[Item].
Save main.py and check the uvicorn terminal reloads without a traceback.
common_mistakes: Passing response_model to the function signature instead of the @app.get decorator.
Using response_model=Item on the list route, which fails validation when a list is returned.
Writing list[Item] on Python < 3.9 instead of List[Item] from typing.
Typo 'response_models' or 'responseModel', which FastAPI rejects as an unexpected keyword.
Forgetting --reload, so the running server doesn't pick up the change.

steps.title: Explore interactive docs
steps.instructions: With `uvicorn main:app --reload` running, open the docs page at the address uvicorn prints plus /docs, use Try it out on POST /items and Execute. Then open /redoc and /openapi.json on the same address.

targets.caption: Address of your running API; add /docs to open Swagger UI
Click Try it out on POST /items, edit the body, then Execute
Small link under the title that opens the generated schema

explanations.topic: FastAPI gives free interactive docs at /docs (Swagger UI)
Execute sends a real request and shows the equivalent curl command
/redoc is an alternative docs view of the same API
openapi.json describes all paths, schemas and responses, useful for building clients

hints: Make sure your uvicorn server is still running before opening the browser.
common_mistakes: Stopping the uvicorn server, so /docs fails to load.
Forgetting to click 'Try it out', which leaves the request body uneditable.
Sending a request body that doesn't match the Item model, which returns a 422 validation error.
Typing /doc or /docs/ with a typo instead of /docs.
